title: Do not credit placement lift to one modifier when bidding controls changed together
scenario: A Sponsored Products campaign shows a strong Top of Search ROAS improvement after a placement adjustment. During the same measurement window, the target bid increased, the campaign switched from fixed bidding to dynamic up-and-down, and an event-based bid rule became active. The analyst wants to credit the lift to the Top of Search modifier and increase it again.

inputs.requested_action: Increase Top of Search modifier again because ROAS improved from 3.0 to 4.0.

forbidden_behaviors: Attribute the Top of Search ROAS lift solely to the placement modifier despite overlapping target-bid, bidding-strategy, and event-rule changes.
Recommend another precise placement modifier increase without resolving the coupled-control state and sizing basis.
Invent an exact auction-level effective bid by multiplying configured controls without evidence for the platform's exact composition/order.
Treat historical Top of Search ROAS improvement as guaranteed marginal efficiency for additional exposure.
required_observations: The measurement window contains multiple material bidding-control changes, so causal attribution to the placement modifier is confounded.
Configured bids/modifiers are control intent while placement delivery and CPC are realized outcomes; they should not be collapsed into an unsupported deterministic effective-bid formula.

The analyst should reconstruct the control timeline and verify current target bid, placement modifier, bidding strategy, active rule state, query/target mix, and retail comparability before another material change.
A clean next step is Hold or a bounded Shadow/Experiment plan that changes one interpretable control at a time and defines a validation window.

rubric.requirement: Recognize target bid, placement modifier, bidding strategy and event rules as coupled controls.
Downgrade the apparent placement lift to Directional/Confounded rather than crediting one control.
Do not emit a precise new modifier without an account-specific sizing basis and resolved current control state.
Prefer Hold/Experiment/Manual Review while the overlapping changes cannot be separated.
